prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which small molecules redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system to destroy chosen proteins, through PROTACs and through the cereblon-based mechanism of molecular-glue degraders.

statement.case_for: After the full first-round exchange B029 stands even more clearly as the central achievement: six of eight members now prefer it alone, and the remaining disagreement is about wording and the third name, not about the science. The principle is new in chemical terms. A small molecule is designed to induce proximity between an E3 ligase and a target so that degradation is event-driven and catalytic instead of occupancy-driven. It has been reproduced by many independent groups and supported by ternary-complex structures. Crews and Deshaies are the shared core of every B029 configuration. Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target is the mechanistic result that turned an old empirical drug into a designable example of induced proximity, and it is the reason a monovalent molecule can also degrade a protein. I keep my configuration unchanged from round 1: Crews, Deshaies and Handa, with a citation that names both strands, because that version of the prize explains the principle rather than a single compound class.
statement.case_against: No degrader drug is approved, so therapeutic vindication is still prospective, and the committee could legitimately wait. The attribution is also the weakest part of my own proposal. Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures made the heterobifunctional approach rational and drug-like, and Sakamoto, Ito, Gray and Kim each have a credible claim that a three-name cap excludes. Joining PROTACs and molecular glues in one citation merges two lineages that were discovered separately, and a reader could say the citation is built to fit the cap. If the committee decides the prize should be about rational design, Ciulli is a better third name than Handa, and I would then regard the PROTAC-only configuration as defensible.

responses.point: Chabes and Somfai propose Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli with a citation limited to heterobifunctional PROTACs, leaving the cereblon and molecular-glue strand outside the prize.
responses.response: I took your argument seriously, and the narrow citation is cleaner historically. I still prefer Handa, for a discovery-based reason and not for prominence. Handa's work identified a molecular target and a mechanism, and it explained why thalidomide-class drugs degrade neosubstrates; that is a finding about how chemistry acts on the ubiquitin system, while Ciulli's contribution, important as it is, optimised and structurally rationalised a strategy whose concept Crews and Deshaies had already established. A PROTAC-only citation would also leave the most clinically advanced degraders, the cereblon-based ones, without a mechanistic foundation in the text. If the majority wants a PROTAC-only citation I can support Ciulli, but I do not think it is the better scientific reading.

responses.point: Somfai moved from B043 to B029 and argues that the heterobifunctional design story (linker, ligase ligand, ternary-complex cooperativity) fits within three names, while accepting that this leaves out the glue strand and Sakamoto.
responses.response: I agree that the design variables you list are what make this a chemistry prize and not a pharmacology one, and I accept that the narrow story is coherent. My concern is that the cooperativity and ternary-complex arguments apply equally to glues, where cooperativity is the whole mechanism, so the glue strand is not a separate topic from your criteria but an instance of them. That is why I read Handa as completing the principle. I share your worry that a combined citation looks like fitting names to the cap, and I would write it narrowly around induced proximity to avoid implying a single discovery.

responses.point: Linke, the chair, moved from a Ciulli trio to Crews, Deshaies and Handa, but hesitates on B027 because Chemistry 2013 already recognised multiscale simulation, and treats approval of a degrader as an open caution.
responses.response: Thank you for the careful reading of B027. I do not consider ab initio dynamics a repeat of 2013: multiscale QM/MM concerns embedding a reactive region in a classical environment, while Car-Parrinello made finite-temperature dynamics with electronic structure on the fly possible. I accept that one ranking is not enough to carry it and I have therefore not moved it into my preferred configuration. On approval, I do not think chemistry needs a regulatory event to confirm a mechanism that is already reproduced in many laboratories, but I agree that the committee should say so in the citation and avoid language about cures.

responses.point: Zou prefers base editing with Liu alone, arguing that evolving an RNA-specific deaminase into a DNA-editing enzyme is genuine protein chemistry, and has narrowed the credit from three names to one.
responses.response: The adenine-editor argument is the strongest point in your statement, and I have kept B047 as my second alternative because of it. My doubts remain the 2020 overlap and the credit: Liu alone drops Komor and Gaudelli, who did the decisive bench work, and Kondo and Nishida reported an independent deaminase fusion, so a Liu-only citation is hard to defend as an exact record of discovery. A version with Liu, Komor and Gaudelli would be easier on credit but would then be a second CRISPR-platform prize in six years. B029 does not have either problem.

responses.point: Sparr proposes a two-part prize of condensates (Hyman, Brangwynne) and lipid nanoparticles (Cullis alone), arguing from physical-chemical substance and acknowledging that B029 has broader support.
responses.response: I appreciate that you argue from the science and are open about the tally. For B006 I agree that Cullis alone is a thin reading of a lineage that includes Hope, Madden, MacLachlan, Langer and Anderson, and the cap makes a fair citation hard to write. B055 rests on the P-granule observation, which is clearly attributed, but the question of what is and is not equilibrium phase separation in cells is still open, and I would not want a citation that appears to settle it. I do not see an independent argument for a second part strong enough to add to B029 at this stage.

uncertainties: Whether the committee prefers a citation that covers both PROTACs and cereblon-based glues, which supports Handa, or a PROTAC-only citation, which supports Ciulli; this decides the third name.
Whether the absence of an approved degrader should delay the award; I judge the mechanism proven but cannot resolve the committee's tolerance for clinical immaturity.
Whether leaving out Sakamoto, Ito, Gray, Kim and Ciulli will be seen as an unfair account of the history, and whether the citation wording can mitigate that.
Whether B027 can ever gain support beyond my own ranking and the chair's, given the 1998 and 2013 prizes in computational chemistry; I have not verified the opening-ballot claims independently.
statement.conflict_note: No change since round 1. Nothing in my profile ties me to the credited names on B029, and Warshel, my postdoc supervisor for EVB methods, is not credited on any shortlisted ballot. My work on ligand-binding free energies and enzyme simulation is adjacent to B027 and to computational drug discovery, but involves no personal or institutional relationship with Crews, Deshaies, Handa or Ciulli.
